metadata.source: State DMF Portals — Maharashtra DMF Trust Annual Reports + DMFT Rules 2015
metadata.coverage: Maharashtra mining districts (Coal, Iron Ore, Manganese, Limestone)
metadata.note: DMF amounts based on royalty inflows from Mines Act 1957, DMFT Rules 2015. High-priority works = 60% minimum allocation; low-priority = 40% maximum

districts.key_gap: Low fund utilisation — 52% corpus unspent despite high mining activity. Critical drinking water and health infrastructure projects stalled.
63% corpus unspent. Tribal-majority district with acute infrastructure deficit — Aspirational District status. DMF severely underperforming vs. need.
Above-average utilisation but 32% unspent. Opportunities in peri-urban and rural cluster development.
53% unspent. Coal Vidarbha belt — significant CSR co-investment opportunity in water and primary health.
Farmers' distress district. 56% DMF unspent. CSR alignment with agri-distress interventions possible.
Balanced utilisation but baseline indicators remain weak. Health and WASH gaps persist.
Moderate utilisation. Tiger reserve proximity — eco-village and tribal livelihood CSR potential.
Half corpus unspent. Tribal-adjacent district with NFHS-5 gaps in child nutrition and women's health.

state_summary.note: Maharashtra DMF average utilisation remains below 50% — significant capital available for co-investment with CSR funds. MPs should prioritise DMF convergence in DPR preparation.
